parsed.use_case: Extracting the most compact text snippet from a long document or web page that contains all required terms from a user's multi-word search query. This enables search engines to display the tightest, most contextually dense preview snippet that satisfies every search constraint.
system_examples: Apache Lucene — Generating search result highlight snippets by identifying the smallest contiguous text span that encompasses all matched query terms.
Splunk — Isolating the tightest chronological sequence of log records that encompasses a full set of correlated diagnostic error markers during incident investigation.
parsed.explanation: The optimal solution uses a sliding window with two pointers and frequency hash tables to dynamically expand and shrink the candidate range in O(|s| + |t|) time. Compared to the naive O(|s|² · |t|) brute-force check over all substrings, this linear-time approach allows search highlighters and stream processors to evaluate megabyte-sized texts in milliseconds without introducing request latency spikes.
